tone.quote: A few Panoan languages have been described as having contrastive high and low tones, specifically Chakobo (Prost, 1960: 8, 1962: 111, 1967: 64), Kapanawa of the Tapiche River (Loos, 1969: 186ff.), and Amawaka (Russell, 1958; Russell and Russell 1959). Unlike tonal languages in the vicinity, like Tikuna, Bora, and Witoto, in all Panoan languages where they have been described, these contrastive tones play only a minor role. Panoan tones appear to be recent innovations specific to these Nawa languages, rather than a proto-Panoan feature (see Loos, 1999b: 230).

tone.quote: Apresenta uma fonologia relativamente simples e destaca-se por ser uma das únicas línguas, ao lado de Kaxarari, a apresentar fonema lateral no interior da família Páno. Seu acento é previsível e recai, até onde se sabe, sempre na última sílaba (a mais a direita) da palavra.
tone.translation: It has a relatively simple phonology and stands out as one of the only languages, alongside Kaxarari, to have a lateral phoneme within the Pano family. Its stress is predictable and falls, as far as is known, always on the last (rightmost) syllable of the word.
